relations.definition: Unauthorized access to a system or network by digital means.
relations.embedding_query_text: hacked: Unauthorized access to a system or network by digital means.

chosen_property.label: hackedBy
chosen_property.definition: An unauthorized access relation between a software application and the corporation responsible for the breach.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly captures unauthorized access by a corporation to a software application; minting 'hackedBy' to represent this specific relation.

candidates.label: hasDigitalDocumentPermission
candidates.comment: A document permission relation between a digital document and an associated access permission. Also called document access, permission for document, document rights. Examples: "A digital document has a digital document permission to read.", "The file has a digital document permission for editing.", "This document has digital document permissions for public viewing."

candidates.label: permissionType
candidates.comment: A categorical attribute indicating the specific type of permission granted within a digital document permission. Also called access level, authorization type, privilege type. Examples: A digital document permission has a permission type of 'ReadPermission'. A digital document permission has a permission type of 'WritePermission'. A digital document permission has a permission type of 'CommentPermission'.

candidates.label: grantee
candidates.comment: A grantee relation between a digital document permission and the audience, contact point, organization, or person to whom the permission is granted. Also called: permission recipient, authorized party, beneficiary. Examples: "Document Access Permission" grantee "Team Members", "File Sharing Permission" grantee "John Doe", "API Access Permission" grantee "Developer Organization".

candidates.label: availableChannel
candidates.comment: A means of accessing a service. Also called: service access, contact channel, delivery method. Examples: "Service 'Customer Support' availableChannel 'Phone Line'", "Service 'Online Banking' availableChannel 'Website'", "Service 'Consultation' availableChannel 'Physical Location'."

candidates.label: isAccessibleForFree
candidates.comment: An access cost relation indicating whether a creative work, event, or place can be accessed without charge. Also called free access, no charge, complimentary access, free of cost. Examples: A public park has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. An online article has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. A concert has isAccessibleForFree set to 'false'.

candidates.label: permissions
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the permissions required for a software application to function. Also called access requirements, app permissions, authorization needs. Examples: A mobile app requires permissions for 'full internet access'. A software application requires permissions for 'access to camera'. A game requires permissions for 'storage access'.

candidates.label: accessMode
candidates.comment: An access mode relation between a creative work and the human sensory or cognitive system through which its content can be perceived. Also called perceptual mode, sensory access, content modality. Examples: "A video's access mode is 'visual'.", "An audiobook's access mode is 'auditory'.", "A text document's access mode is 'textual'."

candidates.label: digitalSourceType
candidates.comment: A source classification relation between a creative work and an IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration code indicating the nature of its digital source(s). Also called: digital origin type, source media type, digital asset source. Examples: "News Photo" digital source type "OriginalDigital", "Archival Document" digital source type "DigitizedAnalog", "Scanned Artwork" digital source type "ScannedPrint".

candidates.label: hasGS1DigitalLink
candidates.comment: A GS1 digital link relation between an offer, organization, place, or product and its associated GS1 digital link URL. Also called GS1 link, digital link, product link. Examples: "A product has a GS1 digital link for traceability.", "An organization has a GS1 digital link for its profile.", "The offer includes a GS1 digital link."

candidates.label: accessModeSufficient
candidates.comment: A sufficient access mode relation between a creative work and a list of access modes that are adequate for understanding its full intellectual content. Also called sufficient perceptual modes, adequate access methods. Examples: "A captioned video's sufficient access modes are 'visual' and 'textual'.", "A podcast with a transcript's sufficient access modes are 'auditory' and 'textual'."

relations.definition: Created or designed a system, tool, or model.
relations.embedding_query_text: developed: Created or designed a system, tool, or model.

chosen_property.label: creator
chosen_property.justification: The 'creator' property matches the Corporation → SoftwareApplication signature, indicating the corporation created the software application.

candidates.label: tool
candidates.comment: A tool relation between instructions or a direction and an object used but not consumed during the performance. Also called instrument, implement, equipment. Examples: "HowTo tool 'hammer'", "HowToDirection tool 'screwdriver'", "Recipe tool 'mixing bowl'". Distinct from instrument, which is a more general property for any object used in an action.

candidates.label: model
candidates.comment: A model relation between a product and its product model or textual identifier. Also called: product model, version, type. Examples: "Smartphone model 'iPhone 15 Pro'", "Car model 'Toyota Camry'", "Laptop model 'MacBook Air M2'".

candidates.label: instrument
candidates.comment: A tool or means relation between an action and the object used by an agent to perform that action. Also called tool, means, device, implement, apparatus. Examples: A writing action uses a 'pen' as its instrument. A cooking action uses a 'knife' as its instrument. A painting action uses a 'brush' as its instrument. Distinct from object, which is the primary entity acted upon, not the tool used.

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: dateCreated
candidates.comment: A temporal origin relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was created or added. Also called: creation date, date of origin, initial date. Examples: "Painting" date created "1889-05-01", "Blog Post" date created "2023-03-15T10:00:00Z", "Data Feed Entry" date created "2023-01-01". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first public release.

candidates.label: author
candidates.comment: An organization or person who created content or a rating. Also called: creator, writer, originator, composer. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Novel' author 'Jane Austen'", "Rating 'Product Review' author 'Consumer Reports'", "CreativeWork 'Article' author 'New York Times'". Distinct from artist, which is typically for visual or comic art.

candidates.label: trialDesign
candidates.comment: A trial design relation between a medical trial and the specific methodology or structure of the trial. Also called study design, experimental design, trial methodology. Examples: "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'RandomizedControlledTrial'", "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'ObservationalStudy'", "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'DoubleBlindTrial'".

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

relations.definition: Shares comparable characteristics with another entity.
relations.embedding_query_text: similar to: Shares comparable characteristics with another entity.

chosen_property.label: similarTo
chosen_property.definition: A relation indicating that a cybersecurity breach shares comparable characteristics with a system misconfiguration event.
chosen_property.justification: The 'isSimilarTo' candidate does not support CybersecurityBreach → SystemMisconfigurationEvent; minting 'similarTo' to capture the relation.

candidates.label: isSimilarTo
candidates.comment: A functional resemblance relation between two products or services that share similar characteristics or purposes. Also called similar to, comparable to, analogous to, like. Examples: Product A isSimilarTo 'Product B' (a competitor's product). Service X isSimilarTo 'Service Y' (an alternative service). A specific brand of coffee isSimilarTo 'another brand of coffee'. Distinct from isRelatedTo, which is a more general association without implying functional similarity.

candidates.label: bioChemSimilarity
candidates.comment: A biochemical entity that is similar to another biochemical entity, often based on fingerprint similarity algorithms. Also called: biochemical analog, similar compound, structural analog. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Compound A' bioChemSimilarity 'Compound B'", "BioChemEntity 'Molecule X' bioChemSimilarity 'Molecule Y'."

candidates.label: additionalProperty
candidates.comment: An additional property relation between an entity (e.g., product, offer, place) and a property-value pair describing a characteristic not covered by specific schema.org properties. Also called extra characteristic, custom attribute, supplementary detail. Examples: "A product's additional property is 'waterResistance: IP68'.", "A place's additional property is 'historicalSignificance: high'."

candidates.label: sameAs
candidates.comment: A URL that identifies the same real-world entity as the item, providing an unambiguous reference to its identity. Also called equivalent to, identical to, linked identity, canonical URL. Examples: `Person: Albert Einstein` sameAs `Wikipedia URL`, `Organization: Google` sameAs `Official Website URL`, `Product: iPhone` sameAs `Wikidata URL`. Distinct from `url`, which is a general URL for the item, not necessarily an identity link.

candidates.label: relatedDrug
candidates.comment: A related drug relation between a drug and other drugs that are similar or commonly prescribed alternatives. Also called alternative drug, similar medication, related medication. Examples: "A pain reliever has a related drug 'ibuprofen'.", "An antidepressant has a related drug 'SSRI'.", "A blood pressure medication has a related drug 'diuretic'."

candidates.label: geoEquals
candidates.comment: A geo equals relation representing a symmetric spatial relationship where two geometries or places are topologically identical, sharing the same interior and boundary without intersecting each other's exterior. Also called: identical to, same location as, equivalent geometry. Examples: "City Boundary A" geo equals "City Boundary B (updated)", "Park Outline (old)" geo equals "Park Outline (new)", "Country Shape (vector)" geo equals "Country Shape (raster)".

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. Examples: "A BioChemEntity has a representation as a chemical structure.", "The entity has a representation as a text sequence.", "This biochemical entity has a URL representation."

candidates.label: amenityFeature
candidates.comment: An amenity feature relation between an accommodation, floor plan, lodging business, or place and a characteristic or service it offers. Also called facility, service, characteristic, convenience. Examples: "A hotel room's amenity feature is 'free Wi-Fi'.", "The apartment's amenity feature is 'gym access'.", "A park's amenity feature is 'playground'."

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

chosen_property.label: participant
chosen_property.justification: The 'participant' property fits the SystemMisconfigurationEvent → Corporation signature, indicating the corporation's involvement in the event.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: question
candidates.comment: A question relation between an ask action and the specific question being posed. Also called asked question, inquiry. Examples: "An ask action involves the question 'What is the capital of France?'.", "A survey asks the question 'How satisfied are you with our service?'.", "A forum post poses the question 'How do I fix this error?'."

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: step
candidates.comment: A component relation between a how-to guide and a single instruction, section, or creative work that forms part of the process. Also called "instructional step", "how-to instruction", "process step", "guide step". Examples: "The recipe has step 'Chop vegetables'", "The guide's step is a video tutorial", "This how-to includes a step for assembly.". Distinct from steps, which refers to a collection of steps.

candidates.label: duringMedia
candidates.comment: A during media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL representing the circumstances while performing this direction. Also called "instructional media", "step-by-step video", "visual guide". Examples: "How-to direction 'Attach part A' duringMedia 'Video of assembly'", "Direction 'Stir mixture' duringMedia 'Image of stirring technique'".

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: foodEstablishment
candidates.comment: A food establishment relation between a cook action and the specific place or food establishment where the cooking occurred. Also called: cooking location, restaurant, kitchen. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food establishment "Gourmet Restaurant", "Home Cook makes dinner" food establishment "My Kitchen", "Baker bakes bread" food establishment "Local Bakery". Distinct from foodEvent, which is a specific event.

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

relations.definition: Constitutes a component or instance within a broader category.
relations.embedding_query_text: part of: Constitutes a component or instance within a broader category.

chosen_property.label: isPartOf
chosen_property.justification: The 'isPartOf' property matches the CybersecurityBreach → CybersecurityBreach signature, indicating the breach is part of a broader category of breaches.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: parentService
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a broadcast service and a broader broadcast service it is a variation or component of. Also called belongs to, is a variation of, is part of, is a channel of. Examples: BBC One Scotland is a parent service of BBC One. A regional news channel is a parent service of a national news channel. A specific sports channel is a parent service of a broader sports network.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: subStructure
candidates.comment: A component relation between an anatomical structure and the smaller anatomical structures that comprise it. Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". Examples: "The heart has subStructure atria", "The brain's subStructure includes the cerebrum", "This anatomical structure is made up of several subStructure elements."

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: ingredients
candidates.comment: A component relation between a recipe and the individual food items or substances required for its preparation. Also called components, recipe items, constituents, elements. Examples: A cake recipe lists 'flour' as an ingredient. A soup recipe lists 'carrots' as an ingredient. A cocktail recipe lists 'gin' as an ingredient.

candidates.label: subTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger trip and a smaller trip that is a component or segment of it. Also called "trip segment", "part of trip", "daily itinerary", "trip leg". Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: members

candidates.label: includedComposition

candidates.label: includedRiskFactor

candidates.label: rsvpResponse

candidates.label: dateReceived
candidates.comment: A temporal arrival relation between a message and the date/time it was received by the recipient. Also called: reception date, message arrival time, delivery time. Examples: "Email" date received "2023-10-26T10:25:00Z", "Package Notification" date received "2023-10-26T11:00:00Z". Distinct from dateSent, which is when the message was dispatched.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: ccRecipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation for a message, indicating a contact point, organization, or person who is copied on it. Also called "carbon copy recipient", "copied to", "CC'd party". Examples: "Email message ccRecipient John Doe", "Internal memo message ccRecipient HR Department".

candidates.label: pregnancyWarning

candidates.label: announcementLocation
candidates.comment: An announcement location relation between a special announcement and the specific civic structure or local business it pertains to. Also called relevant location, associated place, specific venue. Examples: "A special announcement's announcement location is 'City Hall'.", "The emergency announcement's announcement location is 'Local Grocery Store'." Distinct from spatialCoverage, which is used for larger geographic regions.

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: warning

Examples: "Drug warning 'May cause drowsiness.'", "Drug warning 'https://fda.gov/drug-warnings/xyz'", "Medication warning 'Do not exceed recommended dose.'".

candidates.label: issuedThrough

candidates.label: possibleComplication

Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: associatedArticle
candidates.comment: A news article linked to a media object. Also called: related article, accompanying article, news story link. Examples: "MediaObject 'Video of Protest' associatedArticle 'NewsArticle on Protest'", "MediaObject 'Photo of Event' associatedArticle 'Article about Event'."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

An organization knowsAbout 'renewable energy policy'. A researcher knowsAbout 'quantum physics'. candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: skills
candidates.comment: The competencies, knowledge, or abilities possessed by a person or organization, or required for a job or occupation. Also called competencies, abilities, qualifications, expertise. Examples: `Job Posting: Software Engineer` skills `"Python, Java, SQL"`, `Person: Jane Doe` skills `"Project Management, Public Speaking"`, `Occupation: Doctor` skills `"Diagnosis, Patient Care"`. Distinct from `qualifications`, which are formal requirements.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: teaches
candidates.comment: An educational relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is designed to teach. Also called "educates on", "imparts knowledge of", "instructs in", "covers topic". Examples: "The course teaches 'Algebra'", "The learning resource teaches problem-solving skills", "This event teaches advanced programming concepts."

candidates.label: knowsLanguage
candidates.comment: A language proficiency relation between an organization or person and a language they are able to communicate in. Also called speaks language, fluent in, understands language, conversant in. Examples: A person knowsLanguage 'English'. An organization knowsLanguage 'Spanish'. A diplomat knowsLanguage 'French' (fr).

candidates.label: proficiencyLevel
candidates.comment: A proficiency level relation between a technical article and the skill level required to understand its content. Also called skill level, required expertise, target audience level. Examples: "A Python tutorial has a proficiency level of 'Beginner'.", "A deep learning research paper has a proficiency level of 'Expert'.", "A guide to advanced calculus has a proficiency level of 'Intermediate'."

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

relations.definition: Originated from or resulted from a specific cause.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: sourcedFrom
candidates.comment: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: originatesFrom
candidates.comment: A vessel from which a lymphatic structure originates or receives afferents. Also called arises from, derived from, source vessel. Examples: "Lymphatic Vessel A originatesFrom 'Capillary Bed X'", "Thoracic Duct originatesFrom 'Cisterna Chyli'", "Lymphatic Capillary originatesFrom 'Interstitial Fluid'". Distinct from runsTo, which describes the destination.

candidates.label: infectiousAgent
candidates.comment: A causative agent relation between an infectious disease and the specific microorganism or pathogen that causes it. Also called causative organism, pathogen, disease agent, etiological agent. Examples: Influenza has an infectiousAgent of 'Influenza virus'. Tuberculosis has an infectiousAgent of 'Mycobacterium tuberculosis'. Malaria has an infectiousAgent of 'Plasmodium falciparum'. Distinct from infectiousAgentClass, which specifies the *type* of agent (e.g., bacteria, virus).

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

relations.definition: Executed or carried out by an entity.
relations.embedding_query_text: performed by: Executed or carried out by an entity.

chosen_property.label: provider
chosen_property.justification: The 'provider' property matches the SystemMisconfigurationEvent → Corporation signature, indicating the corporation performed the event.

candidates.label: actionProcess
candidates.comment: An action process relation between an action and the step-by-step instructions or method by which it was carried out. Also called execution method, procedure, how-to guide. Examples: "A 'bake cake' action's action process is a recipe.", "A 'repair car' action's action process is a repair manual."

candidates.label: howPerformed
candidates.comment: A performance method relation between a medical procedure and a description of how it is carried out. Also called procedure steps, method of procedure, execution details. Examples: "A medical procedure has a description of how it is performed.", "The surgery details how it is performed.", "This procedure outlines how it is performed."

candidates.label: provider
candidates.comment: A provision relation between an action, work, program, or service and the organization or person that supplies or performs it. Also called supplied by, performed by, offered by, produced by. Examples: "A parcel delivery is provided by FedEx.", "A financial incentive is provided by the government.", "A medical service is provided by Dr. Smith."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: instrument
candidates.comment: A tool or means relation between an action and the object used by an agent to perform that action. Also called tool, means, device, implement, apparatus. Examples: A writing action uses a 'pen' as its instrument. A cooking action uses a 'knife' as its instrument. A painting action uses a 'brush' as its instrument. Distinct from object, which is the primary entity acted upon, not the tool used.

candidates.label: performTime
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the duration required to execute instructions or a direction, excluding preparation time. Also called execution time, active time, task duration. Examples: A recipe's instructions have a perform time of 'PT30M'. A DIY project direction has a perform time of 'PT2H'. A workout routine has a perform time of 'PT45M'. Distinct from prepTime, which is the time to prepare supplies.

candidates.label: byArtist
candidates.comment: A performance relation between a music album or recording and the music group or person who performed it. Also called "performed by", "artist of", "featuring artist". Examples: "Album 'Thriller' byArtist Michael Jackson", "Recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' byArtist Queen". Distinct from composer, which is the person who wrote the music, whereas byArtist is the performer.

candidates.label: replacer
candidates.comment: A replacer relation between a replace action and the entity that performs the substitution. Also called new item, replacement item. Examples: "A replace action involves a replacer 'new battery'.", "A document update uses a replacer 'version 2.0'.", "A software upgrade uses a replacer 'modern system'.". Distinct from replacee, which is the entity being replaced.

candidates.label: agent
candidates.comment: An agent relation between an action and the organization or person who directly performs or drives it. Also called performer, doer, initiator, actor. Examples: "A 'write book' action's agent is 'John Doe'.", "A 'deliver package' action's agent is 'Delivery Service Inc'."

candidates.label: workPerformed
candidates.comment: A performed work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is enacted or presented live during the event. Also called enacted work, live presentation, staged work. Examples: TheaterEvent workPerformed "Hamlet", ConcertEvent workPerformed "Symphony No. 5", DancePerformance workPerformed "Swan Lake". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPresented, which is specifically for movies at screening events.

candidates.label: locationCreated

Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: firstPerformance

Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: founder
candidates.comment: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: primaryPrevention

Also called preventative measure, initial prevention, prophylactic therapy. Examples: A medical condition has a primary prevention of 'vaccination'. Heart disease has a primary prevention of 'healthy diet'. Infection has a primary prevention of 'hand washing'.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
